change.title: pr-37429-flat
change.description: Add HTML sanitizer for translated message resources
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Admin UI shows raw placeholders for error-invalid-multivalued-size
findings.body: The English value was changed from the i18next form to `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus an ICU `{2,choice,...}` clause. The admin UI loads this file through i18next with default `{{ }}` interpolation (js/apps/admin-ui/src/i18n/i18n.ts:16-18 sets only escapeValue). Sibling keys in the same file use `{{0}}` (line 2994). User-profile server errors are translated with `t(key, {...params})` (js/libs/ui-shared/src/user-profile/utils.ts:64-90), so the placeholders are printed literally and the choice clause is shown as text. Restore `{{0}}`, `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`. If a singular/plural form is wanted, use i18next plural keys (`_one`/`_other` with `count`) rather than ICU. The account-ui file has the same change (line 188).

findings.title: Account UI shows raw placeholders for error-invalid-multivalued-size
findings.body: Same change as the admin file: `{{0}}` became `{0}` and an ICU choice was added. The account UI uses i18next with default interpolation (js/apps/account-ui/src/i18n.ts:25-29), and PersonalInfo passes `t` to UserProfileFields (js/apps/account-ui/src/personal-info/PersonalInfo.tsx:117-120), so the multivalued-size error would show `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` and the raw choice text. Restore the `{{n}}` placeholders and the previous wording, or use i18next plural keys.

findings.title: Lithuanian login OTP step 1 replaced by Italian text
findings.body: The new `loginTotpStep1` value is the Italian string from messages_it.properties:92, character for character. The Lithuanian text it replaces was correct. Lithuanian users now see Italian on the TOTP setup page. Replace it with a Lithuanian sentence that says the same thing as the English source at themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties:128 ("Install one of the following applications on your mobile:").

findings.title: Lithuanian account OTP step 1 replaced by Italian text
findings.body: Same problem as the login file: `totpStep1` is the Italian string from messages_it.properties:138. Restore a Lithuanian translation of the English source at themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/account/messages/messages_en.properties:150.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file contains Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The new `totpStep1` uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式, 之一). The rest of this file is Simplified (for example line 110, 配置的认证者). Use Simplified characters, e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：

findings.title: Missing English counterpart or unreadable file throws RuntimeException out of verify()
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() throws RuntimeException at lines 70 and 79. verify() only catches IOException (line 52), so the exception escapes ThemeVerifierMojo's loop (misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/ThemeVerifierMojo.java:45-56). The build then fails with a stack trace, and the messages already collected for other files are lost instead of being reported in the MojoFailureException. Collect these as entries in `messages` (or throw MojoExecutionException from verify()) so the run reports every problem.

findings.title: Verifier allowlist differs from the runtime sanitizer
findings.body: The verifier allows only br, p, strong, b (plus anchors handled separately, lines 58-61). The runtime sanitizer in services (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/theme/KeycloakSanitizerPolicy.java:158-164) allows a much larger set, including span, em, i, ul, li, div. Translations that the runtime would render safely will fail this check if their English uses such tags. Is the narrower policy intended, and if so, should the difference be documented? If the policy should match, the verifier needs a shared dependency.

findings.title: Exact string equality forces churn in translations
findings.body:
The check fails whenever the sanitizer output differs from the input string byte for byte (line 99). Valid markup such as `
` or `` therefore fails. That is why this PR rewrites about 60 translation lines from `
` to `
`. Comparing after normalising the markup would remove this churn. This is a design choice, so it is for the author to decide.

findings.title: Naming and unused parameters
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` is misspelled (line 150). The `key` parameter of `santizeAnchors` (line 150) and `getEnglishValue` (line 164) is unused. `POLICY_SOME_HTML`, `POLICY_NO_HTML` (lines 58-63) and `HTML_TAGS` (line 139) are non-static, non-private instance fields. Policies are rebuilt for every file the verifier visits. Make them `private static final`.

findings.title: No test covers a valid translation
findings.body:
Every new test asserts that a message is present (`hasItem`). Nothing checks that a correct translation produces no messages, such as one using `
`, `` or a matching `` where the English uses HTML. A false positive in the allowlist would go unnoticed. Add a passing fixture and assert the list is empty.

contracts.action: verify-theme now runs the HTML and anchor check on every messages_*.properties file
contracts.before_after: Before: only the duplicate-key check ran per file. After: the HTML check also runs and appends to the same messages list.
contracts.visible_effect: The install build fails with 'Validation errors: [...]' listing the offending keys (ThemeVerifierMojo.java:54-56).
contracts.failure_mode: A RuntimeException from a missing English counterpart (line 79) or an unreadable file (line 70) escapes verify(), because only IOException is caught (line 52). The build fails with a stack trace and the messages collected for other files are lost.

contracts.action: policy.sanitize(value) with commons-text unescape, a new call into the OWASP library
contracts.before_after: Runtime: decodes entities up to five times, then sanitizes with the broad KeycloakSanitizerPolicy. Verifier: a single unescape, a narrow allowlist, and exact equality against the input.
contracts.visible_effect: None at runtime. The check runs only at build time.
contracts.failure_mode: Valid markup that differs from the sanitizer's canonical output is reported as an error (see the churn finding).

summary:
**Batch 1 of 1.** test

**Batch 1 of 1, retry.** Reviewed the verifier change (VerifyMessageProperties.java and its tests and fixtures) and the translation and message changes in this part. Four fix-level findings: Lithuanian login and account OTP step 1 now contain Italian text, the Simplified Chinese account file contains Traditional Chinese text, and the two JS English files have `{0}`/ICU placeholders that i18next does not interpolate (the admin file is at line 3138, the account file at line 188). Consider-level findings cover the exception path in verifySafeHtml, the narrower verifier allowlist versus the runtime sanitizer, exact-equality churn, naming and instance-field cleanup, and the lack of a passing test. Limits: I did not read every properties file in full; I checked the diff hunks and ran targeted greps and reads on the lines behind each finding. The docs/adr directory does not exist at head, so there was nothing to check against ADRs. Nothing was built or run.
